description: The named predicates of the release role. This file is the only definition; the release SOPs cite an id and never restate the test. Every predicate is evaluated against live state at the moment of the step that cites it.

Q-SIG.definition: The task context carries a recomputable proof_root, and every lane verdict supplied to the release carries a recomputable proof_root.

Q-POLICY.definition: Every lane verdict's policy_digest and control_set_sha equal the live values in the gate-control record. A mismatch is drift and refuses the merge; it is never downgraded.

Q-VERDICT.definition: Every lane in the release set has a recorded verdict with verdict PASS, and each verdict.task_id is named by the release capability.
evidence: recorded lane verdicts: verdict, task_id, head, tree
release capability: lane set, capability ids

Q-LANEHEADS.definition: git state (head, tree) for origin/lane/a and origin/lane/b equal the head and tree of their respective PASS verdicts. A lane that moved after its audit is stale; it is not merged.
evidence: git state: origin/lane/a head and tree
git state: origin/lane/b head and tree
recorded lane verdicts: head and tree

Q-CLEAN.definition: The integration worktree is clean before reconcile: worktrees.reconcile refuses a dirty tree, and the harness samples the same cleanliness state before the push.
evidence: git status on the spec-comp worktree
worktrees.reconcile refusal on a dirty tree

Q-STATE.definition: After reconcile, refs/heads/spec-comp and its tree equal the release head and tree returned by worktrees.reconcile, and the merged tree later equals the audited integration tree.
evidence: git state: refs/heads/spec-comp head and tree

Q-METHOD.definition: The merge method is the merge commit set by files/policies/ci.json.merge_method; gh pr merge reads that value and passes --merge at the pinned head. There is no admin, auto-merge, squash, rebase, or bypass option. FF-only applies to lane sync, never to this promotion merge.
evidence: gh pr merge: merge method applied, merge_sha, merged_tree
files/policies/branch-protection.json: required_linear_history=false (a merge commit is allowed)

Q-BASE.definition: The PR's base is files/policies/ci.json.promotion_branch, server-side; gh pr create requires head and title, and its optional body is descriptive only (it never sets the base). The baseRefOid returned by gh pr create equals the live promotion_branch tip and is recorded, not compared to capability.base.

Q-PROT.definition: A fresh gh api branch protection call for files/policies/ci.json.promotion_branch at the PR base OID returns verified=true, matches_policy=true, refusal_code=null, protected=true, and observed_head equal to that base OID. Its normalized required_contexts are the mapped product-ci GitHub contexts, and strict, enforce_admins, allow_force_pushes, allow_deletions, required_reviews, conversation_resolution, and required_linear_history equal files/policies/branch-protection.json. A 404 ("Branch not protected") is PROTECTION_MISSING, any setting difference is PROTECTION_MISMATCH, and a moved base is STATE_MISMATCH; each refuses. The policy file's live_verified/verified_at/response_sha256 is a historical observation, never a substitute for the fresh call, which must be re-run immediately before merge.
evidence: gh api branch protection: protected, required_contexts, strict, enforce_admins, allow_force_pushes, allow_deletions, required_reviews, conversation_resolution, fetched_at, response_sha256

Q-PRHEAD.definition: The PR's headRefOid returned by gh pr create equals the release head that git push just pushed.

Q-GUARD.definition: When capability.task_kind is DRAIN, the guard test named by capability.guard_ref is present at the lane verdict head, is not skipped or xfailed, and passes in that verdict's SUITE result. Its absence or skip refuses the release.
evidence: recorded lane verdict: SUITE result and test node state

Q-CHECKS.definition: Every required id in files/policies/ci-required.json is accounted for at the release head: every github_check_map entry with source product-ci names a real GitHub check that is present and SUCCESS in the single gh pr checks run; every factory-gate id carries a harness-computed check proofs ref for the same head; no required id has source unmapped. gh pr merge re-reads the composed release result and refuses unless those product-ci SUCCESS entries and factory-gate evidence refs are present. A failed check is CHECKS_FAILED, a pending or timed-out watch is CHECKS_TIMEOUT, and a missing mapped name or unmapped id is CHECKS_UNMAPPED. None of them is cleared by a second watch on the same head. A deployment workflow that is red while files/policies/ci.json.deployment.disabled_variable is not true is environmental residual, not a required-check failure and never a CHECKS_FAILED; when deployment is enabled, its red check is CI_FAILED.
evidence: files/policies/ci-required.json: required ids and github_check_map (source, names, command)
gh pr checks: one run per head, gh pr checks name/state/link per mapped product-ci name, missing/unmapped ids
recorded proof store release record (release_record_ref) with a harness-computed check proofs_ref per factory-gate id
